description: Composite of four bright-field TEM micrographs of Fe–28Mn–9Al–1.2C–(0,6)Cr austenitic low-density steel strips after tensile fracture. Every panel carries a 500 nm scale bar (bottom-left) and yellow text/arrows reading "Slip bands" pointing at the banded deformation structure. A yellow value in the top-right corner of each panel gives the average slip-band spacing: (a) as-cast 0Cr = ~90nm, (b) annealed 0Cr = ~190nm, (c) as-cast 6Cr = ~80nm, (d) annealed 6Cr = ~60nm. (a) and (c) show fine, closely and fairly regularly spaced parallel slip bands traversing the grain interior with dark dislocation tangles and small dark precipitates between them; (c) also contains a large lighter, less-deformed region in the lower right. (b) shows much more widely spaced bands (~190 nm) with mottled, heavily dislocated contrast, and (d) shows the finest, densest band set crossing a grain together with a dark wavy band. There are no plotted axes. Together the four panels make the group's argument: annealing widens slip-band spacing in 0Cr steel (90 → 190 nm) but narrows it in 6Cr steel (80 → 60 nm), so the Cr content, not annealing per se, controls slip localisation after tensile fracture.

observations.observation: All four panels are bright-field TEM micrographs of slip bands, each with a 500 nm scale bar, a yellow 'Slip bands' text label with yellow arrows, and a yellow spacing value printed in the top-right corner.
The printed spacing value is ~90nm in (a), ~190nm in (b), ~80nm in (c) and ~60nm in (d).
Panel (c) contains a large lighter (electron-transparent, less-deformed) region in its lower-right quadrant that is absent from (a); panel (d) contains a dark wavy band crossing the field.
The caption states the panel identities: (a) as-cast 0Cr steel strip, (b) annealed 0Cr steel strip, (c) as-cast 6Cr steel strip, (d) annealed 6Cr steel strip, all after tensile fracture.
The citing text states the average spacing between slip bands is ~90 nm and ~80 nm in as-cast 0Cr and 6Cr strips respectively, matching the ~90nm and ~80nm printed on panels (a) and (c).

The citing text states that after tensile fracture the average spacing of the 0Cr strip increases to ~190 nm while that of the 6Cr strip decreases to ~60 nm relative to the as-cast strips, matching the values printed on panels (b) and (d).

The citing text states, as a statistical measurement, average slip-band widths of 13.4 nm and 12.5 nm in as-cast 0Cr and 6Cr strips and 20.5 nm and 7.9 nm in annealed 0Cr and 6Cr strips; these widths are not printed on the images themselves.

The citing text states that average slip-band width is inversely correlated with slip-band spacing after tensile fracture, and terms the finer-band/smaller-spacing state dynamic slip band refinement (DSBR).

The citing text states that annealed 0Cr strip contains more κ-carbides with an average diameter of 14 nm in austenite, versus 8 nm in as-cast 0Cr strip, and that dislocations can only pass through κ-carbides smaller than 10 nm.

The citing text states that the as-cast 6Cr strip has the lowest total elongation despite having the lowest κ-carbide content and smallest size, attributed to its higher dislocation density before stretching.
No κ-carbide particles, dislocation densities or phase labels are individually annotated in any of the four panels; only the slip bands are marked.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM micrograph of as-cast 0Cr steel strip after tensile fracture; 500 nm scale bar; yellow arrows and text 'Slip bands' mark closely spaced parallel slip bands; yellow annotation in the top-right corner reads ~90nm, the average slip-band spacing.

TEM micrograph of annealed 0Cr steel strip after tensile fracture; 500 nm scale bar; yellow 'Slip bands' label with two arrows pointing to widely separated bands; top-right annotation reads ~190nm; contrast is mottled with heavy dislocation tangles.

TEM micrograph of as-cast 6Cr steel strip after tensile fracture; 500 nm scale bar; yellow 'Slip bands' label and three arrows marking parallel slip bands; top-right annotation reads ~80nm; a large lighter, less-deformed region occupies the lower-right of the field.

TEM micrograph of annealed 6Cr steel strip after tensile fracture; 500 nm scale bar; yellow 'Slip bands' label and arrows marking the finest, densest banding; top-right annotation reads ~60nm; a dark wavy band crosses the field.

unreadable_items: No quantitative slip-band width values are printed on any panel (widths appear only in the citing text).
Individual κ-carbide particles and dislocation configurations are not resolvable/annotated at the supplied resolution.
